mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, discretionary trips are suppressed and retail visitation falls further over the next four weeks. The latest pattern shows broadening stay-at-home behavior, which should transmit into lower RETAIL_REC on a 4-week lag.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying below -40 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +15 for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A further weekly drop in TRANSIT below the recent trough predicts fewer in-person shopping trips in the following one to two weeks because access frictions rise immediately. This mechanism is short-lag and should move RETAIL_REC downward when transit mobility breaks to new lows.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60 and is lower than the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 1-2 weeks after TRANSIT crosses below -60 and continues falling week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM do not rise materially, household time reallocates toward local and home-based activity rather than discretionary retail. That substitution should reduce RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 and both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM remain near or below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stay below -45 and TRANSIT stays below -55 for two consecutive weeks, the city is effectively in a high-restriction mobility regime that suppresses retail trips with a two-week lag. Under that regime, RETAIL_REC should continue to move lower.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -45 and TRANSIT below -55 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 2 weeks after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below the stated thresholds for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility relative to the prior week indicates weather- or season-driven outdoor substitution away from indoor retail, which should depress RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks. This effect is strongest when PARKS improves while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 1-2 weeks after PARKS rises by more than 5 points while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain weak.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable or slightly negative while RETAIL_REC drops sharply, households are not substituting toward routine essential trips and are instead cutting nonessential outings. That pattern should keep retail activity subdued for the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays between -20 and -10, indicating the current retail slump was transient.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken together, the joint signal captures a synchronized reduction in commuting and errands that spills into retail. The interaction should forecast a lower RETAIL_REC level within four weeks more reliably than either series alone.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to underperform over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain at or below their current low levels and RESIDENTIAL keeps rising.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES below the recent local minimum signals a fresh tightening or persistence of workplace constraints, which should translate into lower retail mobility over the next two weeks. The effect is strongest when TRANSIT is also deteriorating.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -46 and sets a new 2-week low
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 2 weeks after WORKPLACES breaks below -46, especially if TRANSIT also continues to worsen.
